subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A 'vector' image is one that...
options: Is made of pixels and blurs when enlarged
Uses mathematical paths so it scales without losing quality
Can only be black and white
questions.explain: Vector graphics use mathematical paths, so they can be scaled to any size without pixelation.

questions.q: What does adding black to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding black to a colour produces a shade (a darker version), whereas adding white produces a tint.

questions.q: What is a 'logo'?
options: A symbol or mark that identifies a brand
A full page of body text
questions.explain: A logo is a distinctive symbol or wordmark used to identify and represent a brand.

questions.q: What is a 'maquette'?
options: A small preliminary model of a sculpture
questions.explain: A maquette is a small-scale model made to plan and test ideas for a larger sculpture.

questions.q: 'Saturation' in an image describes...
options: The intensity or purity of the colours
questions.explain: Saturation measures how vivid or intense the colours are; low saturation looks washed out.

questions.q: A 'personal response' (final outcome) should...
options: Be unrelated to your earlier work
Bring together your research and development into your own resolved piece
questions.explain: A personal response resolves your investigations and development into your own meaningful final outcome.

questions.q: Which natural fibre comes from the cocoon of the silkworm?
questions.explain: Silk is a natural protein fibre produced by silkworms when they spin their cocoons.

questions.q: Cubism is most associated with which two artists?
questions.explain: Cubism was pioneered by Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque in the early 20th century.

questions.q: Wool is a natural fibre obtained from...
questions.explain: Wool is a natural animal fibre sheared from the fleece of sheep.

questions.q: 'Product design' is the discipline of...
options: Designing functional objects people use, such as appliances and furniture
questions.explain: Product design develops functional, manufactured objects, balancing how they work and look.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
Write an essay with no images
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.

questions.q: Which artist is closely linked to Impressionism?
questions.explain: Claude Monet was a founder of Impressionism, famous for paintings such as his water lilies.

questions.q: Which group are considered warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm colours, while blues, greens and violets are cool.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To list the cost of materials
To fill empty space with decoration
To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.

questions.q: In photography, 'cropping' an image means...
options: Cutting away parts of the frame to improve composition
questions.explain: Cropping removes unwanted edges to tighten or rebalance the composition.

questions.q: When analysing an artwork, which is the best opening focus?
options: What you can see and how the formal elements are used
How long it took to frame
questions.explain: Good analysis starts by describing what you see and how line, colour, tone and composition are used.

questions.q: A fast shutter speed is most useful for...
questions.explain: A fast shutter speed freezes rapid action, capturing it as a crisp, sharp image.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a sketchbook in GCSE Art?
options: To record ideas and show development of work
questions.explain: A sketchbook records observations, experiments and the development of ideas towards a final piece.

questions.q: Which formal element is described as a mark made by a moving point, having length and direction?
questions.explain: Line is the path of a moving point and is one of the most basic formal elements.

questions.q: What is 'visual' (or implied) texture?
options: The appearance of texture created on a flat surface
Texture you can physically feel on the surface
questions.explain: Visual texture is the illusion of texture on a flat surface, whereas actual texture can be touched.

questions.q: What is the secondary colour made by mixing red and yellow?
questions.explain: Red mixed with yellow produces the secondary colour orange.

questions.q: Shooting from a low viewpoint looking up tends to make a subject appear...
questions.explain: A low viewpoint looking up can make a subject seem larger, dominant or more imposing.
